Rules for AI agents working with MTDI Studio

You are working with MTDI 5.0. If you were asked to use MTDI for a project, read docs/AI.md first and follow it step by step. It covers hardware, firmware, software, computers, networking, cybersecurity and any other field that produces numbers.

  1. Projects are manifests. A project is projects/<id>/project.json here, or mtdi-project/project.json in a repository set up with python -m mtdi adopt. Never add project-specific code to mtdi/.
  2. Pillars stay universal. mtdi/pillars/, mtdi/core.py and mtdi/engine.py must never name a specific sensor, unit, product or field. Everything specific comes from the manifest.
  3. Never invent data. No made-up readings, calibration constants, noise floors or results. Unknown values stay at defaults and are written down as unknown in the project README.
  4. Simulated stays labelled. Simulator data is SIMULATED end to end: never remove the label, never record it, never save it as an environment.
  5. Other repositories are read-only unless the user asks. Inductra Vaion lives in its own repository; projects/inductra-vaion/firmware and bridge/ are byte-identical copies guarded by tests/test_mtdi.py.
  6. Placeholders are generic. Templates and examples meant to be copied say Title, Subtext, Text, Label and Value, never a product word.
  7. Verify before claiming. python -m mtdi check <project>, python -m mtdi run <project> --simulate, python -m unittest discover tests. Report failures as failures, and say what was not tested.
  8. Improving MTDI. If a manifest cannot express what a project needs, change the pillar generically, add a test, keep every project passing, and record it in CHANGELOG.md.
  9. Secrets. Integration tokens (GitHub, Vercel, Notion) come from environment variables only. Never write them into files, manifests or commits.
